images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of the proposed MS-HVED framework.Given any non-empty subset of axial, coronal and sagittal anisotropic stacks, each available orientation is processed by an independent variational encoder that predicts latent multi-scale Gaussian posterior parameters. The resulting orientation-specific latent posteriors are fused voxel-wise using a Multi-Scale Product-of-Gaussians, where per-orientation FOV masks modulate each stack’s precision contribution according to its spatial extent. Samples from the fused latent multi-scale posterior are passed through a shared super-resolution decoder to reconstruct the isotropic HR volume. Optional orientation-specific decoders reconstruct the input stacks.
Figure 2:Reference HR image and qualitative SR results from the IXI[24]and MEN synthetic benchmark datasets. The presented results were reconstructed from5​m​m5mmanisotropic inputs.

Figure 3:Qualitative meningioma reconstructions from real low-resolution stacks.Examples show the available anisotropic clinical input stacks and the corresponding Naive+FOV, SegResNet, and MS-HVED reconstructions.

Figure 5:Representative anatomical observations identified during expert review.Examples show local reconstruction errors that were not necessarily reflected by global image-quality metrics.
(a) Healthy-control case showing reduced conspicuity of the interpeduncular cistern in both reconstructions.
(b) Nigerian case showing reduced distinction between the pituitary gland and clivus in the SegResNet reconstruction.
(c) Nigerian case showing increased signal intensity in the genu of the corpus callosum in the SegResNet reconstruction.
(d) Nigerian0.30.3T case showing reduced separation of the left ICA flow void from adjacent structures in both reconstructions, more prominently with SegResNet.
Arrows indicate the regions discussed by the expert readers.

images.caption: Figure A.1:Expert review interface.Screenshot of the blinded multi-planar review interface used for reference-free clinical evaluation. The interface displays registered LR inputs and anonymised reconstructions side by side, allowing expert raters to inspect axial, coronal and sagittal views before assigning image-quality scores.

Figure A.2:Qualitative comparison on the healthy cohort (real data).Reconstructions are shown for a representative case from the paired healthy-control cohort[13]. Available low resolution (LR) stacks are shown in their inplane and through-plane orientations. Naive+FOV provide non-learned reference baselines obtained by averaging the registered LR stacks with FOV weighting. The separately acquired HR image is shown as a pseudo-reference rather than an absolute ground truth because of contrast differences between the LR and HR acquisitions.

Figure A.3:Qualitative comparison on the Nigerian cohort (real data).Reconstructions are shown for a representative case from the Nigerian clinical cohort[51,52]. Available low resolution (LR) stacks are shown in their inplane and through-plane orientations. Naive+FOV provide non-learned reference baselines obtained by averaging the registered LR stacks with FOV weighting. SegResNet and MS-HVED correspond to the two strongest learned models and are used for the primary expert comparison.

Figure A.4:Qualitative downstream brain-tissue segmentation comparison.A representative SynthSeg[6]segmentation from an IXI-T1 test case is shown for the LR baseline, SegResNet reconstruction and MS-HVED reconstruction, together with the HR reference segmentation.
